title: Production rollout: runtime operational tuning checklist
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
=======
This page is an operational tuning checklist and companion runbook for production model rollouts and routine performance tuning of the Redwood serving runtime. It consolidates cross-cutting checks (kernel scheduling, batching, KV cache, quantization, profiling, canary steps, and monitoring) that should be validated pre-rollout and during live operation.

Purpose
-------
- Provide a reproducible, checklist-driven process for small/medium production changes (model size, quantization profile, batching strategy, shard topology).
- Reduce time-to-detect regressions and ensure SLO alignment (p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost).
- Share concrete commands, dashboards, and rollback criteria for on-call and SRE.

Owner and scope
----------------
- Primary owner: Serving Runtime (runtime-svc) team.
- Secondary owners: SRE, Observability, Model-Onboarding.
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where the runtime binary and orchestration layer are used.

Pre-rollout checklist (gated)
-----------------------------
1) Canary plan drafted and approved
   - Canary % (recommended start: 1%).
   - Traffic routing policy (region-aware, fallback fallback-model).
   - Rollout duration: minimum 24h for steady-state metrics; extend for long tails.
2) Performance smoke tests
   - Run microbenchmarks for target model shape (prompt length distribution).
   - Validate throughput target (TPS) and p95 latency within budget.
3) Kernel & scheduling sanity
   - Ensure kernel mapper selection matches model arch (GELU/FlashAttention variant).
   - Check priority-driven scheduler tags for canary service.
4) Batching and queue configuration
   - Verify max_batch_tokens, max_batch_size, and latency_budget values.
   - Confirm batching policy overrides for high-priority routes.
5) KV cache validation
   - Confirm cache sharding aligns with NUMA topology.
   - Validate prefix cache population strategy and TTL.
6) Quantization profile validation (if used)
   - Run quality regression evaluation on representative prompts.
   - Validate QAT/INT8/FP16 performance delta and check for hallucination increase.
7) Observability and alerts
   - Create/verify dashboards for latency distribution, OOMs, kernel queue length, effective batch sizes, and cache hit ratio.
   - Configure regression alerting: 15% increase in p95 or 5% drop in cache hit ratio triggers oncall.
8) Safety and fallback rules
   - Ensure fallback model variant available and compatibility table updated.

Commands and diagnostics (examples)
----------------------------------
- Start a targeted canary (CLI):
  rdmctl rollout create --service runtime-svc --model-id model-v3-int8 --traffic 1 --duration 24h --route canary-eu

- Run microbenchmark (local):
  ./perfbench --model ./models/model-v3-int8 --seq 512 --concurrency 8 --batch-packing auto

- Inspect runtime scheduler state (prometheus labels available via API):
  curl -s http://runtime-svc.internal/api/v1/scheduler/state | jq

- Dump KV cache stats from a shard:
  rdmctl debug kvcache stats --shard 2 --output json

- Collect GPU kernel traces (short window):
  rdmctl trace start --duration 30s --filters kernel,memcopy && rdmctl trace download --out trace-$(date +%s).zip

Key metrics to validate
-----------------------
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 (global and per-route)
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec by model and route
- Effective batch size: mean and histogram
- Kernel queue depth: per-device and per-priority class
- KV cache: hit ratio, evictions/sec, eviction latency
- Memory: GPU resident set and fragmentation indicators
- Errors: OOMs, model-incompatible exceptions, RPC timeouts

Configuration reference table (common knobs)
--------------------------------------------
Parameter | Typical value | Notes
max_batch_tokens | 2048 | Upper bound on combined token length in a batch
max_batch_size | 32 | Max number of concurrent requests batched together
latency_budget_ms | 120 | Soft SLO for request assembly before flush
scheduler_priority | high/normal/low | High for interactive routes, low for background generations
kv_cache_ttl_sec | 300 | Tune based on prompt reuse pattern
quant_profile | int8/float16/fp32 | Use int8 for cost-sensitive workloads after quality checks

(Represented above as plain text table to keep confluence export-friendly.)

Profiling playbook (when anomaly detected)
-----------------------------------------
1) Identify symptom grouping\   - High p95 with steady p50 -> tail queuing or occasional slow kernels.\   - p50 and p95 both elevated -> overall resource contention (CPU/GPU throttling or batching misconfig).
2) Capture traces\   - Start kernel traces for 60s on affected devices.\   - Collect per-request timing, kernel durations, memcopy times.
3) Check scheduling hotspots\   - Look for priority inversion where low-priority bulk jobs starve interactive queues.
4) Inspect cache behavior\   - If cache miss spike correlates with latency spikes, check shard skew and TTL churn.
5) Quick mitigations (order of ops)\   - Temporarily reduce batch size (max_batch_size -> max(8, current/2)).\   - Raise scheduler priority for interactive routes.\   - Pin affected model shards to different NUMA nodes.\   - If OOMs observed, reduce kv_cache_ttl or decrease model batch packing.
6) Post-mortem actions\   - Add a synthetic workload to test candidate fix before re-enabling full traffic.\   - Update the runbook entry with root cause and long-term mitigation.

Release gating and rollback criteria
------------------------------------
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - p95 latency increase > 25% sustained for 15 minutes.
  - Error rate increase > 3x baseline for 10 minutes.
  - Cache hit ratio drop > 10% with correlated latency increase.
- Manual rollback triggers (owner judgement):
  - Unexplained memory fragmentation growth.\  - Significant model quality regression identified by eval jobs.

Rollout / rollback steps (high level)
------------------------------------
1) Initiate canary with 1% traffic for 24h.
2) Monitor key metrics for 30m stability window then every hour.
3) If anomalies appear, promote mitigations (see profiling playbook).
4) If mitigations fail or rollback triggers hit, revert traffic:\   - rdmctl rollout rollback --service runtime-svc --to stable --reason "p95 regression"
5) After rollback, collect full traces of canary window and open incident ticket.

Dashboards and alert links (examples)
-------------------------------------
- Runtime / Latency Overview: dashboards/runtime/latency-overview
- Kernel telemetry: dashboards/runtime/kernel-telemetry
- KV Cache Health: dashboards/runtime/kvcache-health
- Perfbench trends: dashboards/perfbench/model-trends
- Alerts: alerting/runtime/perf-regressions

Operational run notes and tips
-----------------------------
- For small models, batching tends to dominate latency economics; be conservative when increasing max_batch_tokens.
- Prefer small canaries but run them long enough to exercise tail behavior and daily traffic patterns.
- Use synthetic prompt bundles that mimic real user distributions (include short/long prompts and multi-turn sessions).
- When experimenting with quantization, always run automatic evals tied to the prompt set and check CEILING/LOWER threshold differences.

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them
------------------------------------
- Overpacked batches: can reduce throughput and spike p99 due to stragglers. Test effective batch size distribution.
- Unbalanced shard placement: causes cache skews and cross-node memcopies. Use shard placement tool before rollout.
- Silent kernel fallback: some kernels may fall back to a slower implementation without clear error—check kernel selection logs.

Post-rollout checklist
----------------------
- Confirm steady-state for 72 hours for customer-facing models.
- Record observed effective batch size, kernel mix, and cache hit ratio in the release note.
- Schedule follow-up perf benchmark after 1 week of full traffic.

Appendix: useful commands and scripts
------------------------------------
- Quick effective batch histogram:
  rdmctl metrics query --expr 'histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(runtime_effective_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))'

- Shard placement planner (dry run):
  rdmctl planner plan-shards --model model-v3 --nodes node[1..8] --dry-run

- Kvcache reshard (safe mode):
  rdmctl kvcache reshard --target 8 --grace-period 600 --plan-file plan.json

- Quality smoke eval (small):
  python evals/run_smoke_eval.py --model model-v3-int8 --prompt-set prompts/enterprise-critical.json --out smoke-2026-$(date +%s).json
